chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْهَ وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ ابْنَا نَصِيرٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مُوسَى، عَنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْحَمِيدِ، عَنِ عِيسَى بْنِ أَبِي مَنْصُورٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim, the sons of Nusayr, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Isa ibn Abi Mansur who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ وَذَكَرَ أَبَا الْخَطَّابِ فَقَالَ: اللَّهُمَّ الْعَنْ أَبَا الْخَطَّابِ فَإِنَّهُ خَوَّفَنِي قَائِمًا وَقَاعِدًا وَعَلَى فِرَاشِي اللَّهُمَّ أَذِقْهُ حَرَّ الْحَدِيدِ

translations.en: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) – and Aba al-Khattab had just been mentioned – saying: O Allah, curse Aba al-Khattab, for he made me fearful whilst standing, sitting, and lying on my bed. O Allah, make him taste the heat of the iron.

en.summary: Recorded in Rijal al-Kashshi, this narration highlights the personal enmity between Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and the prominent Kharijite leader Abu al-Khattaw, illustrating the political and theological tensions of the era. The specific invocation for him to 'taste the heat of iron' is interpreted by Shia scholars as a reference to his eventual death by the sword, fulfilling the supplication's literal and metaphorical dimensions. This event underscores the Imam's authority in identifying and condemning key figures of the Kharijite sect who opposed the Ahl al-Bayt.
en.seo_question: What is the meaning of the curse invoked by Imam al-Sadiq against Aba al-Khattab?

key_terms.أَبُو الْخَطَّابِ: Aba al-Kattab, a prominent figure in early Shia history, often associated with the Ghulat sect.
key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ الْعَنْ: O Allah, curse (invocation of divine curse).
key_terms.حَرَّ الْحَدِيدِ: The heat of the iron, a metaphor for death by the sword or intense punishment.
key_terms.فِرَاشِي: My bed/couch, referring to the state of lying down.
